correctness.rationale: The finite model F5[omega]/(omega^2-2) has exactly 515 nonempty faces in sizes 1–5 (25,150,250,75,15), independently consistent with the Brouwer census. Each of 15 tetrahedron/four-simplex removals and 60 triangle/tetrahedron removals is checked to be a valid free-face elementary collapse; final CW dimension is two. The original triangle presentation has 126 edge generators after spanning-tree contraction, and 126 individually legal single-occurrence Tietze substitutions remove every generator with no remaining nonempty relator; this proves pi1 trivial rather than merely H1=0. The Euler characteristic equals 65; a simply connected two-complex has free H2 of rank 64, giving a wedge of 64 S2 by Hurewicz and Whitehead. Independently mod-two signed-boundary ranks are 24,126,60,15. For every one of 600 distinct semiaffine automorphisms, signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz calculations yield exact rational H2 traces; the distribution sums to zero, and the additive Fourier multiplicities are verified algebraically. The actual packaged verify.py is executable and the successful output is embedded. No infinite-family extrapolation.

value.rationale: Paley(25) is the canonical vertex-transitive conference graph on 25 vertices and simultaneously the cyclic order-five Latin-square graph. Published work supplies its ordinary homology, but does not automatically determine the fundamental group or homotopy type. Constructive trivialization of pi1 upgrades known Betti numbers to an integral homotopy equivalence; the full 600-element character and its additive Fourier multiplicity pattern (4,3,2), including absence of global invariants, give substantial new symmetry information. These specific natural invariants are mathematically motivated by the graph’s finite-field affine action and distinguish equivariant topology from merely counting 64-dimensional homology.
